items.note: Plans A and B are byte-identical apart from their title line (checked with diff), so both carry the same steps: S5.1.2 (B1), S5.1.3 (B2), S5.1.4 (B3) and S5.2 (B4). All four match lines 744-764. No sub-step differs.
Both plans have the same S5.3, S5.3.1, S5.3.2 and S5.3.3, which match lines 804-822. There is no difference.

Both have the same S5.4.1-S5.4.6. These carry L3 and L5 and part of L2 (the inclusion <t_X> in t_Y^perp, but not the complement of dimension h-2). Both lack the residual table (L1) and the F_2 orthonormal-basis argument (L4). The coverage is identical, so no sub-step differs.

chain.note: The trees are identical. Each runs S5 (network, labels, s<Wm, tau=1-2^{-50}) to S5.9, S5.10 and S5.11 (power savings), then to S6, S7 and S8 (transforms, recovery, cost table) and on to S0 by the same dependencies. So neither chain thins out or breaks where the other does not.

overall.reason: Plan A and Plan B are byte-identical except for their title line, as a diff confirms, so every step, method and quote is shared. Every item and the chain are therefore tied. Spot checks of the shared steps against the paper (lines 741-1346, 1364-1730, 1885-2590, 2795-3490, 3548-3988, 4040-4995) found no misstatement in either plan.
